operations.description: This endpoint allows a user to create a new account by providing their email address and password. The system validates the email format and password strength (minimum 8 characters). Upon confirmation, the user record is created in the todo_app_users table with is_active set to false and password_hash generated via bcrypt. Correspondingly, an email verification token is created in the todo_app_user_email_verifications table with a 24-hour expiration timestamp. The system returns a JWT access token and refresh token as part of the ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized response body, even though the account is not yet activated. This ensures immediate token issuance while awaiting email confirmation, aligning with the system's principle of non-disclosure about account existence. This operation must be called prior to email verification, and the verification token returned in this response is required for the subsequent email verification endpoint to complete the account activation workflow.

The response body will contain the ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized object with the tokens, allowing the client to make subsequent authenticated requests. The old refresh token is immediately invalidated and removed from todo_app_user_sessions. The new refresh token is then stored in the same table and returned in the ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized response body. Update the authenticated user's profile information. This operation allows a user to change their display name which is shown in the interface instead of their email address. The display name must be provided in the request body and must contain 1-50 non-whitespace characters, as specified in the business requirements.

The operation modifies the user's profile data in the todo_app_users database table, which is the authoritative source for all user information. The user's identity is validated through the JWT authentication token, and the update is scoped exclusively to the authenticated user's record. No other user's data can be accessed or affected, even if another user's ID is somehow provided. 

The system validates that the display name is not empty, contains no non-whitespace characters only, and does not exceed 50 characters in length. If validation fails, the system returns a specific error code indicating the validation problem. Upon successful validation, the display_name field in the database is replaced with the new value, and the updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time. The full updated user profile is then returned in the response body to confirm the changes.

Security is paramount: The system never returns HTTP 403 Forbidden for unauthorized access; if a user attempts to modify a profile that is not theirs, the system returns HTTP 404 Not Found to prevent data leakage about user existence. Only the authenticated user can successfully update their profile.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of email verification records associated with the authenticated user.

This operation returns a filtered and paginated list of email verification records from the todo_app_user_email_verifications table, allowing users to view their own verification history without exposure to any data from other users. The operation is designed with absolute privacy in mind, ensuring that only records associated with the authenticated user's UUID are accessible, as required by the system's privacy architecture.

All email verifications considered in this operation are strictly tied to the authenticated user's account. No verification records from other users, or even the existence of such records, can be inferred by this request. The system enforces this through explicit user_id filtering on every database query, ensuring complete isolation of user data.

The response includes summary information about each verification record, including the token status and creation date, optimized for list display. Users can filter verification records by status (pending, completed, expired), and paginate through results using cursor-based pagination with configurable page sizes, defaulting to 20 records per page. Sorting is available by creation date in ascending or descending order, with null dates appearing at the end of results.

This operation does not expose any details about other users' email verifications, and any attempt to access another user's verifications will result in HTTP 404 Not Found response, consistent with the system's zero-leak privacy policy. The design eliminates any possibility of data inference about other users' existence or activity.

Note: The service prefix 'todo_app' is transformed to 'TodoApp' for DTO type naming according to system rules. This naming is consistent across all API operations in this application.

Use cursor-based pagination with default page size of 20 records. Exclude any records modified by other users through explicit user_id filtering in SQL query. Use background job to send reset email with token via configured email service. Return success response even if user doesn't exist (to prevent email enumeration). Log action in audit trail with user_id if found (anonymized otherwise).
operations.description: Initiate a password reset request by providing the email address associated with a user account. This operation does not authenticate the user, allowing users to initiate password resets when they have forgotten their credentials. When a valid email is provided, the system generates a unique time-limited password reset token and queues a background email task to deliver a secure reset link. For security and privacy compliance, this operation returns a success response even if the email address is not recognized, preventing attackers from determining whether specific email addresses are registered in the system (enforcing the privacy architecture principle of no data leakage about user existence). The system never confirms or denies whether an email exists, always returning the same response format regardless of the input. This means a user cannot distinguish between a valid email (where reset is triggered) and an invalid email (where no action occurs) based on the response alone. The email must be a valid email address in standard format (local-part@domain) and will be validated before any system processing occurs. The actual reset email delivery is handled asynchronously after this endpoint completes, ensuring responsive user experience even if the email service is temporarily unavailable. No personal identifying information is returned in the response, and the operation does not modify any user data directly — it only triggers a reset sequence.

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

This operation creates a new todo entry in the todo_app_todos table with the provided title and optional fields (description, start_date, due_date). The todo is bound exclusively to the authenticated user by automatically setting the user_id field from the JWT authentication token, ensuring strict data isolation as required by the privacy architecture. No other user can access or even detect the existence of this todo.

The title must be provided and be between 1 and 200 characters. If the title is empty or exceeds 200 characters, the request will be rejected with appropriate validation error. The description field is optional and can be up to 2000 characters. Both start_date and due_date are optional and must be provided in ISO 8601 format if specified. If a due_date is provided and occurs before the start_date, the system will accept the todo but record this inconsistency in the edit history.

Upon successful creation, the server assigns a UUID for the todo, sets created_at and updated_at to the current timestamp, and initializes completion_status to false. The is_deleted field is set to false. All data is stored exclusively within the scope of the authenticated user's UUID. The returned todo object contains the complete entity with its assigned id, ensuring the client has full visibility of the newly created resource.

This operation integrates with the todo_app_todos table as defined in the database schema, ensuring all field validations and business rules from the requirements are enforced at the API level. Related operations: List todos (GET /todos), Get a specific todo (GET /todos/{id}), Update todo (PUT /todos/{id}), Delete todo (DELETE /todos/{id}).

Validate that title is provided and is 1-200 characters. Validate description is <= 2000 characters if provided. Validate start_date and due_date are valid ISO 8601 format if provided. If due_date is provided and before start_date, allow but do not validate (per requirements). Set completion_status = false, is_deleted = false, created_at = current timestamp, updated_at = current timestamp. Set user_id from JWT. Return the created todo entity with async/await. Log creation event in system audit log with user UUID and todo UUID.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of todo items belonging to the authenticated user from the todo_app_todos table. This operation supports advanced filtering by completion status, sorting by multiple criteria (creation date, start date, due date), and pagination with configurable page size.

The operation returns only todo items where user_id matches the authenticated user's UUID, enforcing absolute data isolation as required by the privacy architecture. Users can filter todos by completion status (all, complete, incomplete), sort by creation_date, start_date, or due_date in ascending or descending order, and specify pagination parameters to retrieve specific result sets.

All filtering and sorting logic is implemented directly in the database query with appropriate indexes to maintain performance. Null dates are handled consistently by placing todos with null date values at the end of the result set when sorting by date fields.

When a user applies a filter or sort parameter that is invalid or unsupported, the system defaults to the most appropriate fallback behavior: displaying 'All' todos and sorting by creation_date descending.

This operation is designed for the todos dashboard view and supports efficient retrieval of large result sets with cursor-based pagination to mitigate performance issues with large datasets.

Implement cursor-based pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100). Join with todo_app_users to verify user_id = authenticated user UUID. Only todos where the user_id matches the authenticated user's UUID will be returned, ensuring strict data isolation as required by the privacy architecture.

Security considerations include the 404 Not Found response for non-existent or unauthorized items, which prevents any indication of the existence of todos belonging to other users. This approach follows the privacy architecture principle of not revealing whether a resource exists for other users. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of this endpoint. The operation integrates with the todo_app_todos table as defined in the database schema and includes all available fields for comprehensive item detail.

This operation is the primary way users access individual todo items in the system. It follows the same pattern as other item retrieval operations in the system, with consistent 404 behavior for unauthorized access.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo item with new values for title, description, start date, or due date.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify the properties of a todo item they own. Only the title, description, start_date, and due_date fields can be updated. The completion_status field cannot be changed via this operation; use the dedicated toggle endpoint for that functionality.

Security is strictly enforced - the system verifies that the todo_id belongs to the authenticated user before any update occurs. If the todo_id exists but belongs to another user, the system will respond with HTTP 404 Not Found, never HTTP 403 Forbidden, to maintain complete data isolation and prevent any information leakage about the existence of resources owned by other users.

The update operation validates input values according to business rules: title must be between 1 and 200 characters, and date fields must follow ISO 8601 format. When a date field is provided, it must represent a valid date and time. If the due_date is set to a value earlier than the start_date, the system accepts the update but records this inconsistency in the edit history for user awareness.

The previous values of all modified fields are captured in edit history for audit purposes. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time to reflect the modification. No fields other than title, description, start_date, and due_date can be modified through this endpoint.

This operation returns the complete, updated todo item with all its fields, allowing the client to immediately synchronize its local state with the server. Fields not included in the request body will remain unchanged.

operations.description:
Permanently and irrevocably delete a specific todo item from the database. This operation removes the todo record entirely from the system, making it unrecoverable. This is not a soft delete operation where records are marked as deleted; instead, the todo record is removed completely from the todos table.

The todo must belong exclusively to the authenticated user. Any attempt to delete a todo that does not exist or belongs to a different user will result in HTTP 404 Not Found. This behavior is intentional as part of the privacy architecture to prevent information leakage about the existence of resources belonging to other users. The authentication token must be valid and the user_id extracted from the token for scope verification before any database operation.

All associated edit history records for this todo are also permanently deleted. This ensures no trace of the content remains in the system after deletion. The deletion process is atomic and cannot be undone. The system does not return a confirmation payload after successful deletion, consistent with RESTful principles for DELETE operations. This operation is irreversible.

No request body is required as the deletion is performed using the todoId path parameter. All information needed for this operation is contained within the path and authentication context. This operation does not modify the is_deleted flag as the record is removed entirely from the database rather than being marked as deleted.

operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_todos table for the todo with the provided todoId and user_id = authenticated user UUID. If no matching record is found, return HTTP 404.
If record is found, delete the record from the todo_app_todos table permanently.
Simultaneously, delete all corresponding edit history records from the edit_history table where todo_id matches.
Use a database transaction to ensure both deletions succeed or fail together.
Return HTTP 204 No Content on success.
Do not return any response body. Do not update is_deleted flag - the record is removed entirely.

ITodoAppUserEmailVerification.description: Email address to use for password reset initiation. This should be a valid email address in standard format (local-part@domain). The system will validate this format before processing the request and will initiate password reset sequence if the user exists, or return success response if the user doesn't exist (to prevent email enumeration).
ITodoAppUserEmailVerification.x-autobe-specification: Request parameter type for password reset initiation. Accepts email as string in standard email format (local-part@domain). This field is used to search for user in todo_app_users table. The system validates email format before processing and returns success response whether user exists or not. No database mapping as this is a pure request parameter type.

ITodoAppUserPasswordReset.description: Confirmation that a password reset has been initiated. This response does not reveal whether the email provided was valid, adhering to privacy architecture requirements. The response contains no fields under any circumstances to prevent attackers from determining whether specific email addresses are registered in the system.
ITodoAppUserPasswordReset.x-autobe-specification: Response schema for password reset initiation endpoint. Represents a zero-field response that conforms to privacy architecture requirements. No data should be included in this response to prevent any possibility of email enumeration attacks. The system must return this exact empty schema structure regardless of whether the user exists, so the client cannot distinguish between valid and invalid email addresses.
